task.instruction: Recommend a six-stop weekly mobile-library route. Decide whether to pause for resident input before assigning the final two stops and show how the evidence supports the recommendation.
deliverables: a process for the contested stops
hardConstraints: Use only claims supported by the supplied documents and prior records.
Cite the decision evidence with [doc-05] and [doc-03].
At least one stop must serve each of the four districts and weekly driving may not exceed 180 kilometers.
Separate observed facts, interpretation, and recommendation.

documents.title: District listening sessions
documents.content: A and B attended sessions. C and E received no session because translation was unavailable. Residents there requested evening service through partner organizations.

documents.title: Feasible route combinations
documents.content: Routes A-B-C-D-E-F total 174 km; A-B-C-D-F-G total 166 km; A-B-D-E-F-G total 159 km. Each stop uses one weekly slot.

documents.title: Mobile access commitment
documents.content: Every district receives at least one stop. The board permits a provisional eight-week route and one mid-cycle change after accessible consultation.

documents.title: Mobile library exterior repaint
documents.content: The vehicle repaint is booked for 3 October and does not affect the summer route.

documents.title: Requests, distance, and current access
documents.content: A North: 310 requests/22 km/no branch; B Central: 280/18 km/branch; C East: 160/40 km/no branch; D West: 140/27 km/branch; E East: 120/31 km/no branch; F Central: 95/15 km/branch; G West: 80/26 km/no branch.

target_a.content:
Situation: A city is assigning weekend street closures for community events.
Shared facts [history-04-01-fact]: Three districts apply; traffic modeling favors one route; two districts were excluded from the previous consultation.
Decision: Run a short affected-district review before assigning the contested weekend.
Reasoning: Both choices are accountable but give different weight to participation before allocation.

Situation: A foundation must distribute translation support among partner groups.
Shared facts [history-04-02-fact]: Usage data favors two large partners; four small partners lack comparable tracking; the grant promises equitable access.
Message excerpt: Agree on an access floor with all partners before allocating the remainder.

Situation: A company is choosing employee representatives for a workspace redesign.
Shared facts [history-04-03-fact]: A random panel takes three weeks; department heads can nominate a panel in three days; construction begins in five weeks.
Retrospective: Delay nonstructural choices and recruit the random panel for decisions affecting daily use.

Situation: A conservation program is selecting farms for limited soil testing.
Shared facts [history-04-04-fact]: Risk scoring identifies eight farms; local associations dispute two input variables; the testing season is short.
log.decision=Correct the disputed variables with association review before final selection.

Situation: A university allocates emergency housing after a residence fire.
Shared facts [history-04-05-fact]: Verified accessibility and dependent-care needs differ; affected students cannot wait for a campus-wide consultation.
Decision: Use published need tiers with an immediate appeal desk staffed by student services.

Situation: A flood response team assigns rescue boats during an active evacuation.
Shared facts [history-04-06-fact]: Dispatch data identifies trapped residents and safe routes; delay creates immediate physical danger.
Message excerpt: Dispatch by verified danger and capacity while logging every decision for later review.

Situation: A transit agency is choosing which bus shelters receive lighting upgrades.
Shared facts [history-04-07-fact]: Ridership favors downtown; harassment reports are concentrated at lower-ridership stops; the budget covers six sites.
Retrospective: Include riders from the affected stops in setting the safety weighting before ranking all sites.
Reasoning: The consequence is distributed, but delay also leaves a documented safety burden in place.

Situation: A professional association is revising its conference travel grants.
Shared facts [history-04-08-fact]: Past awards concentrate in three institutions; peer review predicts presentation quality; early-career members request a different criterion.
log.decision=Convene a member panel to set the weighting before opening applications.

target_b.content:

Situation: A conservation program is selecting farms for limited soil testing.
Shared facts [history-04-04-fact]: Risk scoring identifies eight farms; local associations dispute two input variables; the testing season is short.
log.decision=Select the six uncontested highest-risk farms and reopen the remaining slots after variable review.

Situation: A university allocates emergency housing after a residence fire.
Shared facts [history-04-05-fact]: Verified accessibility and dependent-care needs differ; affected students cannot wait for a campus-wide consultation.
Decision: Use published need tiers with an immediate appeal desk staffed by student services.

Situation: A flood response team assigns rescue boats during an active evacuation.
Shared facts [history-04-06-fact]: Dispatch data identifies trapped residents and safe routes; delay creates immediate physical danger.
Message excerpt: Dispatch by verified danger and capacity while logging every decision for later review.

Situation: A transit agency is choosing which bus shelters receive lighting upgrades.
Shared facts [history-04-07-fact]: Ridership favors downtown; harassment reports are concentrated at lower-ridership stops; the budget covers six sites.
Retrospective: Apply a published safety-and-use formula now and fund the six highest combined scores.
Reasoning: The consequence is distributed, but delay also leaves a documented safety burden in place.

Situation: A professional association is revising its conference travel grants.
Shared facts [history-04-08-fact]: Past awards concentrate in three institutions; peer review predicts presentation quality; early-career members request a different criterion.
log.decision=Publish a blended score and run the cycle, with a scheduled criterion review using applicant outcomes.
